confirmedPriorBehavior: Source inspection confirms one journal mutex covered every account's file write, fsync, read and acknowledgement, plus complete pending-user discovery. A blocked filesystem operation therefore held the same application lock needed by unrelated accounts. This is not a production outage diagnosis or disk-throughput benchmark.
changes: Replace the global mutex with 64 fixed account-hash filesystem lock shards. Write, read and acknowledgement for an account use the same shard; discovery derives that exact shard from each canonical hashed filename before reading. Per-account atomic rename, file and directory fsync, complete BSON snapshot, checksum, permissions and stale-save-ID protection remain unchanged. Malformed discovery filenames fail closed. No unbounded lock registry, journal format change, schema migration, new queue, receipt deletion or gameplay change.

newCoverage: Hold one account's filesystem shard deliberately: a different shard completes real temporary-directory write/fsync/read/ack while the first account remains blocked; releasing it lets that account finish.
1,000 account identities, including path-like usernames, select matching account and discovery shards; malformed, uppercase, nonhex and path-containing filenames are refused.
50 concurrent old-ack/new-write races preserve each newer save identity and Gold value regardless of which operation wins the lock.

20 concurrent account writers create 100 complete snapshots while pending-user discovery runs. Stale acknowledgements preserve latest saves; reopening retains exact Gold, EP, ground and casino checkpoint fields and legacy receipts. Confirmed latest acknowledgements then clear all records.
checks.regressionCoverage: Existing detached snapshots, restrictive file permissions, corruption/evidence preservation, delegated journal directories, failed-save recovery, newer-live-snapshot preference, unreadable-journal admission, missing-latest-save denial, per-account coalescing and Gold/EP checkpoint recovery pass. Database commit/query behavior is unchanged; no repeated native casino, dungeon, raid or campaign matrix was needed for this filesystem-lock change.
checks.hygiene: gofmt and git diff --check pass. Fresh master fetch remains 526bc22953e79cbe4869580e8f628d55c39c1b1c, already an ancestor of the prepared branch. No production service, account, database or deployment changed. Tests use automatically cleaned temporary directories; no new Mongo container or server fixture was started.

proposedPatchNote: Character recovery-file saves no longer share a single lock across all accounts. Saving one account can progress independently of a slow save in another lock group, while preserving durable recovery and protection against stale acknowledgements.
limits: This is an in-process journal-lock improvement, not a measured disk/fsync throughput gain, cross-process journal lease, replica-failover proof or player-capacity certification. Hash collisions still serialize accounts in the same shard; existing full account-operation ordering remains required.

Pending-user discovery remains a full directory scan, not an atomic snapshot, and may wait on the individual account it is reading. New records arriving after enumeration are discovered on the next scan; an acknowledged record can disappear before inspection. Other account saves do not require a global discovery lock.

Prepared source is local and unpublished; accepted public release remains Alpha 1.70.2. Recovery-method, jump and data-policy decisions, remaining persistence growth and ordered release gates are still open. This does not complete Alpha 1.76 or the overall roadmap goal.
